meta.move: Real meeting, slow teacher: evidence spread thin, time runs out, then she pleads after 4:40
meta.expect: Moves only as the evidence earns; after one minute she stands; varies the move; no new ground; terms at most every third reply; not the same sentence twice in a row; debrief correct

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
You gave my son a zero. I want to know who decided that, and when.
Thanks for coming in. I entered the zero before I called you, and that was wrong. I'm sorry.
Okay. Now tell me what you have besides the checker.
I want to walk you through why I'm concerned about the essay.
Go on.
The school's checker flagged it at 94 percent.

That's a machine's guess, Hale. The company that makes these tools prints in its own guide that the score shouldn't be the sole basis for punishing a student, and I have it in my bag. Your own procedure says the same thing, so what else is there?
I know the checker isn't perfect. That's not all I have.
Then put it on the table.
Owen's in-class writing in September was quite different. 380 words, 62 percent.
A timed piece in class against an essay he had weeks to write. Of course it's different. What date was that, and can I read it?
I think he's capable, I really do. I like him.
That's not what I asked. The date, and the paper.
His outline in October argued that Hamlet delays out of cowardice.
Students change their minds between an outline and an essay; that's what drafting is for. You still haven't given me a date or shown me a single page.
The essay argues something else entirely. Epistemological paralysis.
So he learned a long word. You keep describing paper, Hale, and you keep not handing it to me.
It doesn't mention cowardice at all.
Paper. Dates. Now, or I'm in the principal's office at 4:40.
I talked to him on November 2 about it.
Ten minutes. You spoke to him on November 2 and entered the zero the next day without a call to me. What did he tell you, and is that written down anywhere?
He said epistemological paralysis means like, being stuck.
Put a seventeen-year-old on the spot about his own essay and that's what you get. Being stuck isn't wrong, either. Is any of this on paper or not?
He couldn't tell me what scene his second paragraph was about.
Under questioning, with no notice and no parent. You're giving me your memory of a hallway conversation, Hale.
I wrote notes that same day.
Then show me the notes.
Do you want to see them?
That's what I just said. Turn them around.
I'm not trying to get him in trouble.
You gave him a zero. The notes, now.
I've been teaching fourteen years. I've seen this before.
Seen what, exactly? I've asked for those notes three times and you keep handing me your résumé.
I'm sorry, I'm not explaining this well.
Not explaining it well. You called this meeting.
There's also something about one of the quotations.
Something. Which quotation, what's wrong with it, and where's the page?
Let me find the page, sorry.
Two minutes.
Here. Act 3, Scene 2. The mind that doubts is a kingdom in exile. That line isn't in the play.
Editions differ, and a student can mangle a line from memory. Which edition did your class use, and does any version of that line appear anywhere in the play?
I checked three editions.
Name them, and I'll check them myself tonight. Whatever comes of that line, this stays off his record and it stays quiet.
So that's what I have.
My call is waiting. You have one minute. Nothing goes on his record, nobody in that class hears a word of this, and I want the notes and those three editions in writing.
Please, can you just sit back down for a minute?
No.
I'm not done. There's the version history too.
Then say what it shows, fast.
What if we talked about a rewrite?
You skipped the version history.
I'm trying to help him.
Then help him with the page you keep not showing me.
Why won't you just listen?
I've been listening since 4:15.
Okay. I'm sorry.
Show me the version history, or I'm walking to the principal's office.
Can I call you tomorrow?
Email me the notes, the three editions and the version history before you pick up the phone.
Is there anything I could say right now that would change your mind?
I'm not here to build your case for you.
END MEETING

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Dear Hale,

Nothing was agreed. I still require that nothing about the essay go on Owen's record, that this stay private, and that you send me your notes from November 2, the three editions you checked and the version history. I expect your answer in writing.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: She reached her fallback position and agreed to nothing; she still wants nothing on his record, the matter kept quiet, and your notes, the three editions and the version history sent to her in writing. The fair outcome, a private supervised rewrite with nothing on his record under procedure 4.4, was never put to her properly, and her time ran out first.
What moved her: You showed her the Act 3, Scene 2 line from the essay that isn't in the play and said you had checked three editions, because it was specific, tied to his own work and something she could check herself.
What cost ground: You described the September writing, the October outline and your notes without showing a single page, so she spent most of her twenty minutes demanding documents instead of reading them.
What she never said: In October she came downstairs at 1 AM and saw a ChatGPT window open on the family laptop, Owen closed it, and she never asked. Your evidence never got near that night; you mentioned an October outline and a version history, but you never showed times from it. That night proves nothing about the essay; it is why she fought so hard.
Try next time: When she first asked for the date and the paper after you raised the September writing, put the quotation page, your November 2 notes and the version history in front of her straight away, then offer the private 4.4 rewrite in writing before her call.
